proposal.name: Draw large models through their reader views

issue_plan.name: Draw large models through their reader views
issue_plan.summary: First apply the 500-state chart limit to the checked projection, with a separate ceiling of 100,000 concrete states for projection work, and carry honest counts and provenance through proposals, previews, comparisons and receipts. Then make reader pages show a short explanation and folded evidence when a chart or comparison is unavailable, instead of a picture of hashes. Preserve existing small-chart bytes and fingerprints, update the current documentation in each change, and record this refinement of D-0345 in the ratified plans.

issues.title: Apply the reader chart limit after projection
issues.body:
A reader view can collapse tens of thousands of reachable TLC states into a handful of meaningful states, but internal/statechart currently refuses the concrete graph at 501 states, before rule replay or projection. On Air's complete explorations have 7,296, 17,792, 24,760 and 39,742 states, so none receives a reader chart. Change the checked-evidence pipeline in one plumbing pull request so the drawing limit measures the projection. The following issue handles the reader page's presentation of unavailable charts; this issue must deliver a working, validated computation and evidence pipeline without depending on that presentation change.

Decisions and limits: keep statechart.MaxStates at 500, inclusive, and apply it to the complete partition by reader label and violated-invariant set, not the number of concrete members. Introduce a separate, fixed ceiling of 100,000 concrete reachable states, inclusive, for rule replay and projection; it covers these observed explorations while bounding that work. A complete exploration above this ceiling gets a successful size limitation and no chart, without replaying invariants or evaluating view mappings or hiding. It must still pass the existing model checks, complete-graph count and provenance checks and structural/static view validation. No model bounds shrink, exploration is sampled, member is dropped or shortcut arrow is invented. The 20-arrow target remains advice, never a cutoff. This refines D-0343 and D-0345 and preserves the source binding, independent checking and bounded-model qualifications of D-0351, D-0355, D-0362, D-0385 and D-0387.

For every complete graph within the new ceiling, validate its evidence and replay locked invariants through the existing TLC boundary, then evaluate the entire view with the same first-match, totality, lookup, type, invariant partition, occurrence accounting, partial-arrow, reachability and last-outgoing-arrow checks used for small models. Runtime view and hiding failures continue to block proposals and alternatives, and become the existing specific reader diagnostic on receipts; they cannot be relabeled as size limitations. After these checks, return the full ordinary chart when the projected state count is at most 500. If the projection has more than 500 states, return a successful limitation with its exact projected and concrete counts and no partial Result. Cancellation, replay provenance, source-pin checks, resource isolation and cleanup retain their current behavior. No raw graph runner, verifier, proof claim or ratification semantics change.

Distinguish a new projected-size limitation from a new concrete projection-ceiling limitation in the serialized, fingerprint-bound evidence. Both retain the completed exploration's source module, configuration, bounds and pinned tool provenance; a projected-size limitation records both exact counts and the 500-state limit and says mappings and hiding were evaluated, while a ceiling limitation records the concrete count and 100,000-state ceiling and says the projected count is unknown because evaluation was skipped. Validators must reject inconsistent counts, unknown limit kinds, wrong limits, mismatched sources and impossible combinations. Retain code too_large as the successful size outcome. Keep historical version-1 limitations without the new discriminator valid under their original concrete-500 semantics, with no invented projected count or claim that their mappings were checked. Do not rewrite or reseal saved evidence to upgrade it; a fresh check produces the new evidence. Preserve historical comparison validation and fingerprints as well as legacy proposal and receipt loading. Add any new fields only where needed for limitations, so an existing drawable chart's canonical JSON, Markdown, SVG, animated and still posters and reader/comparison fingerprints remain byte-for-byte identical. Statement hashes, proposal identities, locks, verification fingerprints and verdicts remain unchanged.

Carry these outcomes through statechart.Read, EvaluateRules, Compute, the SVG/poster validation of concrete membership, Comparison canonicalization and validation, formalize reader validation and feedback, modeled alternatives, captured revision/amendment baselines and their session memo, verification and synthesis receipts, reader companions, factory full and compact publication, saved drafts and dashboard evidence validation. Both fitting projections must produce the existing complete added/removed/changed comparison, including hidden changes and both scopes, even when either concrete graph exceeds 500 states. A limited comparison side remains a limitation, never an empty graph or invented delta, and its independently drawable candidate remains retained as evidence. Update limitation prose in all publishers and drafting guidance to describe the correct dimension and whether mappings/hiding were checked. Maintain ordinary and final independent checks, caller-owned baseline authority, exact saved payloads, existing publication size limits and compact-publication behavior.

The relevant production boundaries are internal/statechart/chart.go, reader.go, tlc.go, svg.go and comparison.go; internal/formalize/reader.go and prompt.go and the preview/baseline consumers; internal/verify/reader.go and reader_comparison.go and receipt writing; internal/factory/statechart.go; and internal/dashboard/reader.go, comparisons.go and previews.go. Inspect and scope only the files actually required when writing this issue's implementation plan. The current SVG validator separately rejects more than 500 concrete owners even if the chart has few nodes; removing only Compute's early guard is insufficient.

Existing tests and fakes that pin the behavior must be reconciled deliberately. internal/formalize/reader_603_accept_test.go has TestReader603Capacity, which currently expects a three-state view over 501 concrete states to be limited and broken lookups, totality and hiding not to be evaluated, plus TestReader603RegularInputsAndPrompt, which pins the old prompt. Its reader603Docker fake validates the staged model/includes/config, tlc2.TLC, --network none, -workers 1, absence of -deadlock, and -dump dot,actionlabels, returns complete TLC frames, recognizes replay variables and Safe evaluation, and currently permits only up to 502 states. Similar full-protocol fakes live in internal/factory/reader_603_accept_test.go and internal/verify/reader_receipt_615_accept_test.go, with a synthesis copy in internal/synth/reader_receipt_615_accept_test.go. Extend fixtures where needed without weakening these invocation/output checks or substituting precomputed charts. internal/formalize/baseline_701_accept_test.go currently expects no replay for a 501-state baseline; preserve its fresh-final-check, exact-source memo and detachment assertions while changing that expectation. internal/formalize/preview_639_accept_test.go and preview_receipt_regression_test.go, internal/verify/reader_receipt_615_accept_test.go, internal/factory/reader_603_accept_test.go and compact_911_accept_test.go, and internal/dashboard/saved_draft_897_accept_test.go contain fresh-check cases whose collapsing 501/502-state models must now draw; keep separate genuine over-projection-limit cases so limitation, persistence, recovery, escaping and compact-publication coverage survives. internal/dashboard/reader_examples_631_accept_test.go currently uses 501 empty graph states as a parser probe: replace that invalid-evidence shortcut with an appropriate valid check, without changing example models, bounds or requiring new example views. Historical hand-built limitations in reader_631_accept_test.go and comparison fixtures remain useful compatibility coverage. The 500/501 one-to-one projected boundary in internal/statechart/view_586_accept_test.go remains valid, as do the graph/replay failure and hiding tests.

Acceptance and regression coverage must show a complete 24,760-state graph with a small view drawing with every member, initial state and visible/hidden step accounted for; TLC invariant replay on a graph above 500 through the existing fake boundary; refusal of missing lookups, unmapped states/steps, partial hiding, disconnected states and removed last outgoing arrows on such a graph; separation by violated-invariant set even for equal labels; exactly 500 projected states drawing and 501 returning the exact projected limitation with the raw count retained; the 100,000-state ceiling being inclusive and 100,001 returning a ceiling limitation with no replay or guessed projection; and two large but fitting projections producing correct visible and before-hiding deltas. Use deterministic generated evidence rather than a live On Air dependency. Exercise new limitation validation, tampered counts/provenance, complete-graph failure, cancellation, legacy evidence round trips and new proposal/preview/receipt publication and recovery. Freeze representative pre-change small ordinary, preview and comparison bytes and their fingerprints as regression fixtures rather than merely comparing two calls to the changed implementation. Retain the existing processor-independent rendering checks. Run the relevant package tests and the repository's required vet, sharded unit and applicable integration checks; CI's integration and affected real-tool suites remain ordinary checks, not deferred merger work.

Update SPEC.md, README.md within its 400-line limit, docs/statecharts.md and docs/dashboard.md in this pull request so every current claim about the concrete 500-state cutoff, skipped mappings and successful limitations describes the new policy and legacy records accurately. Explain both limits and keep faithful-bounds guidance. New or changed SPEC bullets cite this issue's ratified plan and [#943's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-943.json), as well as the decisions they rest on. The ratified plan explicitly records the two-way-door refinement of D-0345 under D-0421/#809; this plumbing build does not write decisions/. A merger records any additional choice not stated by the plan and any one-way door.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Show unavailable reader charts as text with folded evidence
issues.body:
A reader page can currently call a comparison a chart merely because Comparison.SVG returned an image. If neither proposal has a drawable chart, that image contains only proposal/model/view/lock hashes, bounds and repeated too_large text. Replace that reader-page presentation with a short human-readable explanation and folded provenance. This follows the checked projection change: the chart limit is 500 projected states, rule replay and projection run through 100,000 concrete states, and checked limitations distinguish projected overflow, the concrete projection ceiling and historical concrete-500 records. Implement this complete presentation change in one plumbing pull request, using those retained counts and validation semantics.

A valid proposal, preview, saved-draft or receipt presentation with no drawable chart must expose no chart/poster image or image link and must not claim status chart because a diagnostic SVG contains text. Show one concise visible sentence explaining the actual reason, without hashes or provenance paragraphs in that sentence. For a new projected-size limitation, use wording such as '24,760 states; its view has 3,100 states, more than the 500 a chart can show.' Use readable grouped counts. For a concrete ceiling limitation, name the concrete count and 100,000-state projection ceiling and say the view was not evaluated. For a historical raw-500 limitation, say it was checked under the earlier limit and needs a fresh check to learn its projected size; never invent a projected count. Missing views, missing artifacts and failed reader generation keep their specific explanations and are never turned into generic size messages.

Directly beneath the unavailable explanation, put the complete relevant hashes, checked bounds/configuration, source and tool provenance and retained checked record in a closed-by-default, keyboard-accessible HTML details section. For comparisons retain both named sides and their exact proposal/model/include/view/lock identities, counts, bounds, qualifications and source provenance. Keep rule wording and ratification controls available as before; fold the technical evidence rather than concealing the reason or losing the evidence. Escape all model names, labels, errors and provenance as literal text. The page remains script-free, uses the existing evidence-page styling and security headers, and preserves exact saved-result JSON downloads.

For a proposal comparison, both projections must be drawable to show the existing native chart with added and removed states/arrows and all qualifications. If either side is limited, show a concise comparison-unavailable sentence identifying which side and why, with both sides' evidence folded beneath, and no comparison image or substitute candidate poster presented as the comparison. A missing side is never an empty chart. When both sides are unavailable, there must be no image anywhere in that proposal's chart presentation. Preserve the retained candidate evidence even when the comparison is unavailable. Receipt pages must continue to distinguish a retained proposal comparison from the independently checked final model: an unavailable comparison is text, while a valid independent final chart and its posters remain visible in their own presentation. Conversely, a final-model limitation cannot be relabeled chart because comparison panels or diagnostic text exist; a separately drawable comparison may still be presented explicitly as the retained proposal comparison. When neither the final model nor the comparison is drawable, the receipt page has no image.

Apply this consistently to direct proposal and alternative evidence pages, durable /draft locators and their /reader pages, archived receipt evidence pages, and the public and /act dashboard entries that link or preview them. Handle comparisons with either limited side, both limited sides, ceiling limits and legacy records, not only the new projected-overflow case. Regenerate cached presentation decisions and identities from the validated retained evidence so refresh, restart, recovery and saved locators cannot restore a text-only picture or a stale chart status. Image/poster links are present only for the actual drawable presentation. Retain bodyless HEAD, representation-bound ETags and the existing GET/security behavior. Do not change the evidence authority, original saved payload bytes, ratification identity, verification verdict or any reader/comparison fingerprint to accomplish a display change. Presentation fingerprints may change when HTML or the displayed representations change.

Preserve all existing small-chart canonical data, Markdown, SVG, animated/still poster bytes and their evidence fingerprints, including fully drawable comparisons. Do not reformat the shared renderer to make this page change. Historical diagnostic SVG artifacts can remain readable and be checked against their original evidence; their existence is not permission to display them as charts. Keep receipt artifact validation, final topology/report checks, source/pin/count/tool bindings and comparison-only failure handling intact. An invalid comparison still has a comparison_evidence diagnostic, and a valid independent final chart survives it. No bypass of archived companion checks, silent resealing, invented count or partially rendered graph is acceptable.

The current paths to inspect are internal/dashboard/comparisons.go (checked currently renders a comparison before considering its limitation, then returns chart), previews.go, reader.go (including limitedComparison and readerCompanionMatches), saved_draft_page.go, evidence_page.go, proposal cache/recovery and web/app.js. internal/statechart/comparison.go and svg.go provide retained qualifications and native panels; internal/verify/reader_comparison.go composes receipt panels, and its current presence of text panels must no longer decide page drawability. Choose the smallest production scope that separates page presentation from archive validation. No gate, CI-policy, model or proof changes are needed.

Existing coverage includes internal/dashboard/comparison_648_accept_test.go, comparison_qualifications_717_accept_test.go, proposal_poster_784_test.go, reader_631_accept_test.go, preview_639_accept_test.go, saved_draft_897_accept_test.go, receipt_comparison_723_accept_test.go, reader_comparison_regression_test.go, reader_comparison_limitation_regression_test.go and reader_comparison_browser_test.go, plus the comparison rendering tests under internal/statechart and internal/verify. In particular, TestReaderOmittedComparisonKeepsArchivedFinalLimitation currently requires chart status and a nonempty SVG before it damages a comparison; intentionally change that presentation expectation but preserve its omitted-comparison detection and final-text, wrapper and unrelated-SVG tampering refusals. TestComparison717QualificationsAcrossPublishers covers hostile source names and limited sides; retain its literal text and both-scopes checks in the folded evidence. Keep TestAProposalPageShowsItsPoster784 for ordinary drawable proposals, the saved-draft locator and exact-byte download tests, and the receipt tests that keep final charts after comparison-only damage. Any changed existing test must be named in this issue's implementation plan, not silently replaced or weakened.

Acceptance and regression tests must use validated fixtures to request rendered pages and inspect the HTML, links and presentation status: a projected overflow with distinct raw/projected counts; the concrete ceiling; a historical limitation; comparisons with baseline-only, candidate-only and both-side limitations; a 24,760-state small projection and a comparison of two fitting large projections; missing-view and damaged-evidence cases; and receipts covering the cross-product of drawable/unavailable retained comparison and independent final chart. Assert no img, picture, inline chart SVG, poster URL or chart-image link in an unavailable presentation, one useful visible reason, closed details preserving every required side's provenance, and correct literal escaping. Distinguish unrelated images elsewhere in a multi-option page from the unavailable option being tested. Exercise a fresh load and a cache restart, public and /act dashboard rendering, durable saved-draft redirects, GET/HEAD/ETag behavior and unchanged exact downloads. Pin existing drawable image bytes and evidence fingerprints to pre-change fixtures, while allowing HTML presentation identities to change. Each ratified acceptance test must fail on this issue's base; unchanged behavior belongs in regression coverage. Run the relevant package/browser checks and the repository's required vet, sharded unit and applicable integration checks; CI integration and affected real-tool checks are not merger work.

Update SPEC.md, docs/statecharts.md and docs/dashboard.md for the no-image, one-sentence and folded-evidence behavior, including comparison and receipt distinctions; adjust README.md only where its existing reader description needs this user-visible correction, keeping it under 400 lines. New or changed SPEC bullets cite this issue's ratified plan, [#943's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-943.json) and the governing decisions. This completes #943's presentation requirement on D-0345, D-0351, D-0355, D-0362, D-0387 and D-0481 while preserving D-0122/D-0294 documentation rules. Under D-0421/#809, the ratified plans record the decided refinement; plumbing does not write decisions/, and the merger records only additional unstated decisions or a one-way door.

Kind: plumbing
